lessons: Structural: the snapshot table was converted from embedded volatile values to fetch-always rows for the four API-served price series. The remaining numbered rows (BoI rate, unemployment, LFPR, GDP, population, minimum wage) have no public JSON API and still need a manual refresh each cycle. If an API for the Labour Force Survey appears, convert those too.

Evidence drift is bidirectional: the unemployment evidence snippet already read 3.1% / July 2026 while the SKILL.md body still said 2.7% / February 2026. A prior cycle refreshed evidence.json without propagating into the body. Next cycle, diff every evidence raw_snippet against the body value it backs, not only the reverse.

The CBS media-release pages (cbs.gov.il/en/mediarelease/.../Consumer-Price-Index-July-2026.aspx) render a title but an empty text body, so they cannot be used as an evidence source URL even though they exist and return 200. Cite the Main Price Indices hub instead.

Expert MINOR deferred: Step 4 still lists 'Average wage by sector (published quarterly)' with no code or table number to reach it; the wage series has no API path. Consider adding the CBS wage table number next cycle.

Deferred over the Phase 4.1 discretionary cap: the Gotchas section does not warn that the apartment price index (40010) sits on a 1993 average base while the CPI (120010) sits on a 2024 average base, so the two index values are not comparable in level. The base-mismatch Troubleshooting row covers the general case but not this specific pairing.
